summary: Iter24 — Re-test of production-hardening suite after iter23's body-parse fix. Reused existing /app/backend/tests/test_iter23_prod_hardening.py (16 cases). Result: 16/16 PASS in 8.57s. Both previously-broken endpoints (POST /api/vault/unlock-verify, POST /api/vault/recovery-redeem) now correctly parse their JSON bodies — they return semantic 404 'Vault not initialised' / 'Recovery code not recognised' instead of the 422 query-param error seen in iter23, AND the slowapi rate limiter correctly fires (429 on 11th unlock-verify call and 6th recovery-redeem call). All other regression items also green: login 200 with admin@acs.in/admin123, login 429 brute-force at 11th wrong-password attempt within 60s, /auth/me with token, /auth/my-clinics, /vault/status returns mode field, vault mode state machine (standard↔vault_pending; direct→vault_enabled rejected with 400), /vault/setup round-trip + 409 idempotency, /patients regression, /appointments regression, /api/health 200, CORS preflight headers present.
critical_code_review_comments: vault.py fix is clean: removed `from __future__ import annotations` and switched body params to `Annotated[Model, Body()]` form. This is the canonical FastAPI pattern when stacking external decorators (slowapi @limiter.limit) on top of routes that also use Depends(...). Manually re-verified via curl: both endpoints now return semantic 404s instead of 422 parse errors.

rate_limit.py proxy_aware_key still uses leftmost X-Forwarded-For — correct for ingress-fronted prod. In-memory store is fine for single-process; if backend ever scales to multiple workers, swap to Redis storage_uri so 10/min budgets are shared across pods (current code allows N×limit in a multi-worker deploy).
server.py login @limiter.limit('10/minute') verified firing at 11th attempt — works as designed.
Test file uses dedicated synthetic XFFs (203.0.113.{10,11,12,55,66,99}) so rate-limit buckets don't bleed across tests — good practice; preserve this pattern for future limit-related tests.

Suggestion (non-blocking): consider adding /tmp/test_vault_e2e.py + /tmp/test_vault_recovery.py into /app/backend/tests/ so the encrypted round-trip + recovery flows are part of CI rather than ad-hoc scripts.
test_credentials: admin@acs.in / admin123 (super_admin on clinic-acs-demo). All XFF buckets isolated; no demo data mutated (vault state machine test tears itself down).
seed_data_creation: None. Vault state-machine + setup round-trip tests tear down any artefacts they create so the demo clinic is left at vault_mode=standard, no clinic_vaults doc.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter23 regression is fully closed. /app/backend/tests/test_iter23_prod_hardening.py is the canonical production-hardening regression suite — re-run it with `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iter23_prod_hardening.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/<name>.xml` whenever auth, rate-limit, or vault routers change. Always wait 60s+ between back-to-back full runs so the in-memory slowapi window resets cleanly; the test file already uses dedicated XFFs (203.0.113.55 / .66 / .99) to isolate buckets.
rca of the issue: RCA from iter23 confirmed and resolved. Original bug: vault.py had `from __future__ import annotations` AND used bare `proof: VaultUnlockProof` body params. With PEP 563 stringified annotations + slowapi's @limiter.limit decorator wrapping the function, FastAPI's signature inspection fell back to query-parameter interpretation for the Pydantic body, yielding 422 'Field required loc=[query, proof|payload]'. Fix applied by main agent: removed the future-annotations import and switched both bodies to `Annotated[Model, Body()]` to force explicit body resolution. Verification: curl POST /api/vault/unlock-verify with valid auth + JSON body now returns 404 'Vault not initialised' (semantic), and 11th call within 60s from same X-Forwarded-For returns 429. Same for /api/vault/recovery-redeem at 6th call. Pytest 16/16 PASS.
